accepted.evidence: Turner places Pashai aṅguṛī and Arang ä̃uṛ in section 2, the *aṅgūḍi branch. Darrai aŋuṛek shares the aŋuṛ stem and finger sense, but its final -ek is not analyzed by this source; the link is to the family, not an exact reconstruction of that ending.

Turner explicitly gives Pashai Darrai kunǰī elbow within the kaphōṇi family, alongside Lauṛi kučī and Laghman kōnči. Lehr Darrai kunci differs in affricate transcription and vowel notation; preserve its spelling while linking the attested family.

Turner explicitly lists Pashai Lauṛi and Arang paṣū rib, with Kuṛangal and Chilas pāṣū, under párśu. Lehr Darrai paśu has the same meaning and stem, with its source sibilant and vowel length left unnormalized.

Turner section 1 explicitly gives Pashai Darrai and Wegal šū̆ṛíṅ dog. Lehr Darrai śoṛiŋ corresponds closely; its original vowel and sibilant notation are retained. The link selects section 1 rather than distinct śunī and *śunakha branches.
